title: The season passes. The caravan comes too late: the year has turned and the standing at ʿArafāt has gone by, the afternoon beneath the Mount of Mercy that is the Hajj itself. The month among the scholars of al-Azhar cost the Emperor the pilgrimage. The caravan disperses and turns for home; the journey must be made again from the beginning

data.event: The Royal Ḥajj: The Season Passed
data.choice: We tarried too long. It must be undertaken again.
data.calendar: the game counts the season as over by 6 January 1386; the chronicle's tabular reckoning had put ʿArafa near 11 January, so the game's Hajj calendar runs earlier than the arithmetic one

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, 6 January 1386

title: Misfortune turns to fortune on the road home: the Emperor recruits many of the scholars of al-Azhar he sat with to fill the halls of the capital. The Jamāʿa must be persuaded to fund them, and the ʿulamāʾ back the measure: sponsor theological seminaries. The Jamāʿa passes it: the realm gains theological seminaries for ten years

data.date: on the way home from the Hajj, early 1386; the day awaits a save
data.outcome: passed (Trent's account): Theological Seminaries for 10 years, +10% research, +0.01 literacy a month, +2 Innovative

title: A second office of the bureaucracy, inspired by the Mamlūk court and the lore of the old caliphates the Emperor met in al-Qāhira: the Ḥijāba, the chamberlainship of Umayyad Qurṭuba, whose ḥājib headed his own council, received petitioners and embassies and drafted decrees in the caliph's name. While the crown pays for it, it strengthens the crown and its legitimacy, and it gives the dīwān another seat

data.precedent: the ḥājib of the Cordoban court, raised under the caliphate of 929; under al-Manṣūr (978–1002) the office became royal power in all but name, centralising rule through the palace at the price of a nobility shut out of the caliph's counsel (the game's text)
data.date: after the Hajj, 1386; the day awaits a save

title: The crown prince Ismāʿīl, nineteen, who ruled as regent through his father's pilgrimage, is brought home from the fleet, where he served as an admiral to carry the crown's authority over the seas, and takes the new seat in the dīwān that the Ḥijāba creates, to help his father fill the capital with scholars

data.seat: the cabinet seat added by the Ḥijāba
data.before: admiral, extending crown control over the seas (Trent)
data.task: the Emperor's scholar-building project, the seminaries and the scholars of al-Azhar (Trent)
